title: Minutes of the Presidents Meeting With the Joint Chiefs of Staff, November 19, 1943, 2 P.M., Admiral’s Cabin, U. S. S. “Iowa”  Present were Roosevelt, Hopkins, Leahy, Marshall, King, Arnold, Brown, and Royal.

United States Delegation Memorandum  The author of this memorandum was presumably Hopkins. Harriman indicated to the editors in 1956 that Hopkins had handed the paper to him to read; that he had added the sentence at the end; and that he had returned it to Hopkins (023.1/5–256).

Memoranda by the Chinese Government  Handed by Wang to Hopkins by direction of Chiang, for transmission to Roosevelt—not as formal proposals but as an indication of the problems which, the Chinese felt, might suitably be discussed, and “as reference material for the committee responsible for the drafting of the communiqué”. This footnote is based on, and the quoted words are taken from, a letter of May 21, 1957, from the Chinese Ambassador at Washington (Tong) to the Historical Office, Department of State (023.1/5–2157). It does not appear that any committee was appointed to draft the communiqué; see post, pp. 399–404.

American Draft of the Communiqué, With Amendments by the President’s Special Assistant (Hopkins)  The draft as typed is the same as the draft submitted to Roosevelt (supra) except for the addition, on a separate sheet, of the last three paragraphs naming the conference participants. The handwritten amendments by Hopkins were made prior to the revised version of November 25, 1943 (infra).

Revised American Draft of the Communiqué  This revised draft was dictated by Hopkins to Warrant Officer Cornelius on the morning of November 25, 1943 (letter from Albert M. Cornelius to the Historical Office of the Department of State, 023.1/3–257). A typewritten notation on one of the carbon copies of this draft reads “11/25/43 edition”.
British Draft of the Communiqué  The handwriting appears to be that of Churchill. Date and authorship not indicated, but the text as amended is very similar to the final version printed post, p. 448.

Final Text of the Communiqué  This is the agreed text as it was given by Hopkins to Kirk on the afternoon of November 26, 1943; see the memorandum by Kirk, infra. For earlier drafts of the communiqué, see ante, pp. 399–404. The communiqué, was released to the press by the White House on December 1, 1943, and was printed, with slight editorial variations, in the Department of State Bulletin, vol. ix, December 4, 1943, p. 393.
Memorandum by the United States Chiefs of Staff

Minutes of a Meeting of the Pacific War Council  The Pacific War Council consisted of representatives of those signatories of the Declaration by United Nations which were fighting in the Pacific. It met from time to time at Washington under Roosevelt as chairman. secret
